content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. My experience spans natural language processing, document classification and production model monitoring, and I would welcome the opportunity to apply it to systems that help merchants and support agents.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents. I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration, and established production quality and data drift monitoring. Our models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts, an experience relevant to Quillstone’s work on support routing. I also built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts as a research project assistant. Alongside my professional work, I am pursuing doctoral research in named entity recognition and hold a master’s degree in computer engineering.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience taking NLP models from research to production could contribute to your Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and appropriately tailored to the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. It uses strong evidence from the candidate's experience, including 94% accuracy across 23 classes, transformer fine-tuning, MLflow, model serving, Azure, and production monitoring. The progression from current role to earlier customer complaint classification is logical and relevant to support-ticket routing. The main content limitation is that it does not explicitly state several supported technical keywords, particularly Python, software engineering, MLOps, and model serving as production engineering capabilities. It also does not directly connect the candidate's experience to the job's responsibilities of building, deploying, and operating AI systems or maintaining data-processing and training pipelines.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter has ATS-friendly plain text structure, standard headings are not required for a cover letter, and the employer, role title, technologies, and relevant outcomes are easy to parse. Keyword coverage is good for NLP, document classification, transformers, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, App Service, monitoring, and data drift. AI screening probability is reasonably strong for the supported requirements, but moderate overall because the letter does not explicitly include Python, MLOps, model serving, software engineering, deployment, operating production systems, or data-processing pipelines. These terms should be added only where they accurately describe the candidate's documented experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the NLP, production ML, model deployment, monitoring, Azure, and customer-support-text aspects of the role. The customer's complaint-topic classification is a credible connection to support routing. The master's degree in computer engineering also meets the education requirement. The candidate's material does not establish experience with chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), feature engineering, or data-ingestion pipelines, so these are genuine qualification gaps rather than wording defects. The material also does not clearly establish four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production; the documented ML Engineer role began in March 2023, while the earlier Data Scientist role documents model development but not production deployment. The letter does not need to claim these unsupported areas.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE: In the second paragraph, revise the sentence beginning "I also introduced MLflow" to make the production-engineering alignment more explicit without adding unsupported experience. For example: "I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration, and deployed Python-based FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service, with production model-quality and data-drift monitoring." This uses supported experience while adding the ATS-relevant terms Python, deployed, production, and monitoring.

MINOR: In the final paragraph, change "my experience taking NLP models from research to production" to "my experience building, deploying, and monitoring NLP models from research through production." This more directly mirrors the role's build, deploy, and operate responsibilities and remains supported by the candidate's documented work.

MINOR: In the paragraph describing the banking role, change "an experience relevant to Quillstone’s work on support routing" to "an experience relevant to Quillstone’s support-ticket topic classification and routing work." This creates a closer, truthful match to the job description's support-routing language without claiming experience with chat assistants or RAG.

My experience spans natural language processing, document classification and production model monitoring, and I would welcome the opportunity to apply it to systems that help merchants and support agents.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents. I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration, and established production model-quality and data-drift monitoring for our deployed Python-based services. Our models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts, an experience relevant to Quillstone’s support-ticket topic classification and routing work. I also built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts as a research project assistant. Alongside my professional work, I am pursuing doctoral research in named entity recognition and hold a master’s degree in computer engineering.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building, deploying, and monitoring NLP models from research through production could contribute to your Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and well structured. It establishes relevant NLP, model deployment, monitoring, Azure, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, and customer-text classification experience without making unsupported claims. The quantified 94% accuracy and 23-class result provide useful impact. The connection between customer complaint classification and Quillstone’s support-ticket work is relevant and credible. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly state the candidate’s more than five years of experience, and it gives limited evidence of software-engineering practices beyond serving and monitoring.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is highly parseable: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional paragraphs, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It includes strong matching keywords such as machine learning, natural language processing, document classification, BERTić, XLM-R, MLflow, model registry, production monitoring, data drift, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, App Service, Python, and customer complaint classification. ATS screening probability is good for the demonstrated requirements. Keyword coverage would improve by explicitly stating the duration of experience and naming Git/version control, while unsupported keywords such as chat assistants, RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, and data versioning should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s core work of building, deploying, and operating NLP/ML systems in production. It demonstrates Azure, Python-based services, MLflow, model serving, monitoring, transformer fine-tuning, text classification, and experience progressing from research to production. The candidate’s customer complaint text classification is a credible adjacent match for support-ticket classification. The candidate material does not show experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, or explicit data versioning; these are genuine requirement gaps rather than wording defects. The letter also does not provide direct evidence related to Quillstone’s culture signals such as ownership, teamwork, candid feedback, or learning from mistakes, although adding unsupported claims about those behaviours would be inappropriate.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the opening paragraph, explicitly state the duration of experience so the four-year requirement is immediately visible. For example, change “My experience spans natural language processing, document classification and production model monitoring” to “With more than five years of experience in natural language processing, document classification, and taking ML models from research and prototyping into production, I would welcome the opportunity to apply this background to systems that help merchants and support agents.”
2. In the second paragraph, make the Python and version-control evidence more explicit using information already present in the CV. After “Our models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service,” add: “I use Python to build these services and Git for version control.”
3. In the final paragraph, replace the general phrase “building, deploying, and monitoring NLP models” with terminology that more closely mirrors the role while remaining truthful: “building, deploying, operating, and monitoring NLP models in production.”

content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. With more than five years of experience in natural language processing, document classification, and taking ML models from research and prototyping into production, I would welcome the opportunity to apply this background to systems that help merchants and support agents.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document classification model that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R for named entity recognition in Croatian documents. I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration, and established production model-quality and data-drift monitoring for our deployed Python-based services. Our models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service. I use Python to build these services and Git for version control.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts. I also built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts as a research project assistant. Alongside my professional work, I am pursuing doctoral research in named entity recognition and hold a master’s degree in computer engineering.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building, deploying, operating, and monitoring NLP models in production from research through production could contribute to your Customer Operations AI team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It presents relevant evidence rather than repeating the CV, including the 94% classification result, transformer fine-tuning, MLflow, model serving, Azure deployment, and production monitoring. The progression from current production work to earlier text-classification and research experience is clear. Its main weakness is that some claims are broad or repetitive, and it does not explicitly connect the candidate’s experience to the engineering practices and customer-support use cases emphasized in the role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings and plain text, contains no problematic tables or graphics, and includes strong supported keywords such as Python, NLP, model serving, MLflow, model registry, monitoring, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, App Service, Git, and production. AI screening probability is moderate to strong for the requirements supported by the candidate’s background. Screening may be weaker for the exact requirements and phrases not evidenced in the candidate information, including chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, CI/CD, automated testing, orchestration beyond MLflow, and data versioning. These should not be added unless they are factually supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s core production-ML responsibilities: it demonstrates NLP model development, fine-tuning, deployment, model serving, monitoring, cloud use, and progression from research to production. It also connects reasonably well to customer-support work through the candidate’s experience classifying customer complaint topics. The candidate’s computer engineering degree, Python experience, Azure experience, and MLflow use are supported. Gaps in the candidate material include demonstrated experience with chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, and data ingestion pipelines. The candidate material also does not clearly establish at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production, although it does establish more than five years of broader NLP and machine-learning experience. The letter does not provide much evidence related to teamwork, learning from mistakes, candid feedback, or service ownership, although mentoring interns can support a limited teamwork and development connection.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ALIGNMENT/CLARITY IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the second paragraph, change “I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registration” to “I also introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and the model registry.” This uses the exact terminology supported by the CV and more closely matches the job ad’s MLOps language.
2. In the second paragraph, change “established production model-quality and data-drift monitoring for our deployed Python-based services” to “established production model-quality monitoring, including data-drift monitoring and weekly reporting, for deployed Python services.” This is more precise and reflects the candidate’s documented responsibilities.
3. In the closing paragraph, remove the repetitive phrase “in production from research through production” and replace the full sentence with: “I would welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building, deploying, operating, and monitoring NLP models could contribute to Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team.” This eliminates repetition while retaining the strongest role-relevant terms.
4. In the third paragraph, make the customer-support relevance more explicit by changing “My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying topics in customer complaint texts” to “At Baranjska kreditna banka, I classified topics in customer complaint texts, giving me directly relevant experience working with support-related language data.” This remains truthful and connects the evidence to the target team.
5. Before the final paragraph, add one short sentence based on the documented mentoring experience: “I also mentor two student interns, an experience that has strengthened my collaborative approach and commitment to knowledge sharing.” This provides limited but truthful evidence relevant to the company’s teamwork and learning culture without claiming unsupported leadership or ownership.
6. In the opening paragraph, replace “systems that help merchants and support agents” with “AI systems that help support organisations classify and route customer requests and assist support agents” only if the intended phrasing is clearly presented as motivation rather than claimed prior experience. Do not state that the candidate has built assistants, routing systems, or merchant-facing products, because those experiences are not present in the candidate information.
